uml.text: U M L, the Unified Modeling Language, has fourteen diagrams. Seven are behavioral: they show what happens. Use case, activity, sequence, state machine, and three more.

struct.text: Seven are structural: they show what the system is made of. Class, component, deployment, object, package, profile, and composite structure.

class.text: The class diagram is the main building block of object-oriented design. Each class is a box with three parts: the name at the top, attributes in the middle, operations at the bottom.

rel.text: Lines between the classes show their relationships.

comp.text: A component diagram zooms out. A component is a modular part of the system, one level above a class.

iface.text: Components talk through interfaces. A provided interface is a full circle: a ball. A required interface is a half circle: a socket.

plug.text: Order requires an item code. Product provides it. The ball fits into the socket.

assembly.text: That link is an assembly connector: one component provides the service another one uses.

delegation.text: A delegation connector links a subsystem's outside contract to the component inside that really does the work.

soa.text: Component diagrams belong to component-based software engineering, and are used especially for service-oriented architecture.
